social-learning.def: Social learning theory (observational learning): learning by watching others and imitating them. It depends on attention, memory (retention), the ability to reproduce the behavior and the motivation to do so.

vicarious.def: Vicarious conditioning: learning from the consequences that happen to a model. Vicarious reinforcement (the model is rewarded) makes imitation more likely; vicarious punishment (the model is punished) makes it less likely.

modeling.def: Observing and imitating a specific person's behavior. Models who are similar, admired or rewarded are imitated more.

insight-learning.def: A sudden understanding of how to solve a problem, reached as a whole rather than by gradual trial and error.

latent-learning.def: Learning that happens without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason (an incentive) to use it.

cognitive-map.def: A mental representation of the layout of a place, formed by exploring it.
